ds.desktop.notify.service

Class NotifyClient

  • java.lang.Object
    • ds.desktop.notify.service.NotifyService
      • ds.desktop.notify.service.NotifyClient

  • public class NotifyClient
extends NotifyService
    A NotifyClient allows to use a notification service running on another process of the host in order to display notifications, just like if the service were running on this process.
    Since:
    0.9 (2019-06-18)

      • postNotification

        public void postNotification(java.lang.String title,
                    java.lang.String message,
                    java.lang.Integer type,
                    java.lang.Integer align,
                    java.lang.Long timeout,
                    java.lang.String themeName)
        Description copied from class: NotifyService
        Posts a new notification to the service, setting the parameters needed for it.
        Specified by:
        postNotification in class NotifyService
        Parameters:
        title - The title to display.
        message - The message to display.
        type - The notification type (0~7).
        align - The text/layout alignment (0,1).
        timeout - The maximum time in milliseconds the notification will stay on screen.
        themeName - Either "light" or "dark", refering to the two stock themes available.
        See Also:
        NotifyService.DARK_THEME, NotifyService.LIGHT_THEME

      • tryAndGet

        protected static NotifyClient tryAndGet()
        Attempts to create a NotifyClient object and polls for any NotifyServer running on this host. If the service is located, the client is kept and returned to the caller.
        Returns:
        A newly created NotifyClient, able to connect to a local NotifyServer running on this host, or null if no service could be located.
